top_story: Renewed fighting in Yemen has sharply worsened a long-running humanitarian collapse, displacing 71,000 children and driving up acute and severe malnutrition as health access and basic services erode. That deterioration lands alongside a formal warning to Save the Children over staff safety failures after the 2023 death of Hisham al-Hakimi, underscoring how aid operations in Yemen remain endangered by both conflict and weak protection practices. In Iran, the death sentences and long prison terms imposed on twins Taraneh and Romina Rahimi for protest activity signal a continued hardening of state repression well after the peak of street mobilization. The regional picture is one of entrenched coercion—through war in Yemen and punitive justice in Iran—deepening civilian vulnerability while narrowing the space for protection and dissent.
